A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a novel neural architecture for QA that can be trained with a small amount of data and can be applied in a wide variety of settings, ranging from QA over text alone to QA over a combination of text and KBs, where it outperforms existing approaches by a large margin.
GRAFT Net can be trained on a small amount of data to extract answers for a broad range of questions from a combination of a KB (with a small number of errors) and text.
GRAFT Net achieves state-of-the-art results on all the datasets, and is the first model that can handle both KBs and text in an open domain QA setting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
early fusion of text and KB is more effective than sequential pipelined approaches, and that a graph based model that can jointly reason over the KB and the text is a promising direction for QA.
a single model that can effectively combine information from both KBs and text can be more effective in practice than specialized models for each modality.
the combination of text and a KB can be used to answer open domain questions in a practical setting, where the KB may not be comprehensive.
